sentences.zh: 所以克里斯提尼所做的是，他将阿提卡的整个乡村，所有的城镇、庄园、村庄，切分成150个不同的区域。

sentences.en: And these districts are called deeMs. Right.
sentences.zh: 这些区域被称为“德谟”（deems）。没错。

sentences.en: And basically, it's from deems rather than from families, Cleisthenes says, that citizens of the democracy are obliged to take their second name.
sentences.zh: 基本上，克里斯提尼说，民主制度下的公民必须从“德谟”而不是从家族中获取他们的姓氏。

sentences.en: So they're not, you know, it's not son of or daughter of, it's the deem that defines where you come from.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不是“某某之子”或“某某之女”，而是“德谟”定义了你来自哪里。

sentences.en: And the only way that you can be enrolled as a citizen of Athens is first by being enrolled within a deem.
sentences.zh: 而成为雅典公民的唯一途径，首先是在一个“德谟”中注册。

sentences.en: And so the effect of this is to completely kind of cut and slice and dice all these kinds of traditional loyalties and create entirely new ones.
sentences.zh: 这样做的效果是彻底切断、分割了所有这些传统的忠诚，并创造了全新的忠诚。

sentences.en: And aristocrats can't afford to be snobby about this because it's the people of a deem who will choose the representatives who go to the assembly.
sentences.zh: 贵族们不能对此表现得傲慢，因为是一个“德谟”的人民将选择去参加公民大会的代表。

sentences.en: So if the aristocrat wants to be chosen as that, you know, he's got to play ball.
sentences.zh: 所以如果贵族想被选中，他就必须配合。

sentences.en: He's got to show respect to his fellow members of the deem.
sentences.zh: 他必须尊重他所在的“德谟”成员。

sentences.en: And so inherently that then builds up a kind of a sense of equality of purpose.
sentences.zh: 这从本质上建立了一种目标平等的意识。

sentences.en: But of course, there's a risk with this that deems might be used as a kind of launchpad for tyranny.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这也有一个风险，即“德谟”可能会被用作暴政的跳板。

sentences.en: So how do you stop that?
sentences.zh: 那么如何阻止这一点呢？

sentences.en: So Cleisthenes has a solution to that as well, which requires making the entire system even more complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯提尼对此也有一个解决方案，这需要使整个系统变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: And I can imagine that listeners are cheering at this.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象听众们对此欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: So basically what he does is he bunches the deems into organizations that are called thirds.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上做的是将“德谟”聚集成被称为“三分区”（thirds）的组织。

sentences.en: And Attica has been divided three ways.
sentences.zh: 阿提卡被分成了三个部分。

sentences.en: And these in turn are then bunched into things that are called tribes.
sentences.zh: 这些部分又被聚集成被称为“部落”（tribes）的东西。

sentences.en: And so the effect of this is basically to ensure that, you know, you have people from one
sentences.zh: 这样做的效果基本上是确保来自阿提卡一个地区的人，

sentences.en: area of Attica are joined with another area of Attica and another area of Attica in a third.
sentences.zh: 与阿提卡另一个地区和再一个地区的人在“三分区”中结合在一起。

sentences.en: And then the thirds in turn are bundled into tribes of which there are 10.
sentences.zh: 然后这些“三分区”又被捆绑成部落，共有10个。

sentences.en: So you have multiple loyalties.
sentences.zh: 所以你有多种忠诚。

sentences.en: And there is no kind of obvious center for anyone to try and construct, you know, an equivalent of a clan.
sentences.zh: 没有任何明显的中心供任何人去构建一个相当于氏族的东西。

sentences.en: So it's a brilliant way of reframing and resetting traditional loyalties.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种重构和重置传统忠诚的绝妙方式。

sentences.en: And the question is, how is this going to work?
sentences.zh: 问题是，这会奏效吗？

sentences.en: And really, it depends on Cleisthenes convincing the Athenians that this very radical, this very novel, this very complicated constitutional framework isn't actually
sentences.zh: 实际上，这取决于克里斯提尼能否说服雅典人，这个非常激进、非常新颖、非常复杂的宪法框架实际上并不是

sentences.en: radical or novel at all.
sentences.zh: 激进或新颖的。

sentences.en: That it's simply giving back to them what they'd always had, that Solon had previously given them, and that Theseus had previously given them.
sentences.zh: 它只是把他们一直拥有的东西还给他们，那是梭伦之前给他们的，也是忒修斯之前给他们的。

sentences.en: And the way that he kind of institutionalizes this is that he draws up a list of ancient Athenian heroes, including Erechtheus,
sentences.zh: 他将此制度化的方式是列出一份古雅典英雄的名单，包括厄瑞克透斯，

sentences.en: including Egeus, people like that, people who had been involved with the kind of primordial beginnings of Athens.
sentences.zh: 包括埃勾斯等等，那些参与了雅典原始起源的人。

sentences.en: And he gives this list of 100 names to Apollo in Delphi, and Apollo chooses 10.
sentences.zh: 他把这份100人的名单交给德尔斐的阿波罗，由阿波罗选出10人。

sentences.en: So there's a sense that this whole system is rooted in the ancient soil of Athenian history,
sentences.zh: 所以人们感觉到整个系统植根于雅典历史的古老土壤中，

sentences.en: and has the approval of the gods, and that Cleisthenes hasn't really had anything to do with it.
sentences.zh: 并得到了众神的认可，而克里斯提尼本人并没有真正参与其中。

sentences.en: So Cleisthenes is not instituted as a kind of, you know, a Rose-Pierre or a Cromwell or a Lenin.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯提尼并没有被塑造成罗伯斯庇尔、克伦威尔或列宁那样的人物。

sentences.en: That's not how he, you know, the memory of him basically gets secluded.
sentences.zh: 这不是人们记忆中他的样子。

sentences.en: It's ancient, it's primordial, it's ancestral, it's always been what Athens is all about, and it's God-given.
sentences.zh: 它是古老的、原始的、祖传的，这就是雅典一直以来的样子，而且是神赐的。

sentences.en: So first of all, is this the first example in history of, or the first known example, of a political transformation being rooted in a kind of invented past?
sentences.zh: 那么首先，这是历史上第一个已知的政治转型植根于某种虚构过去的例子吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's such a common thing, the Norman yoke in the 17th century in England, or the idea that the founding fathers of
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很常见，比如17世纪英国的“诺曼枷锁”，或者认为美国开国元勋们实际上是在忠于某种辉格党或后革命时代的

sentences.en: the United States were actually being true to a kind of Whiggish or post-revolutionary kind of
sentences.zh: 英国政治的观点，或者，你知道，在改革者和革命者中非常普遍的观点，

sentences.en: English politics, or, you know, the idea that is so common among reformers and revolutionaries,
sentences.zh: 即他们实际上并没有做任何新的事情，他们只是在恢复人民古老的自由。

sentences.en: that actually they're not doing anything new, they're just restoring the ancient liberties of the people.
sentences.zh: 克里斯提尼在雅典所做的不正是这样吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that what Cleisthenes is doing in Athens?
sentences.zh: 这是第一次发生这种情况吗？

sentences.en: And is this the first time it's happened?
sentences.zh: 我认为每个古代民族都会这样做。

sentences.en: I think every ancient people do this.
sentences.zh: 罗马人这样做，斯巴达人也这样做。

sentences.en: The Romans do it, the Spartans do it.
sentences.zh: 通过声称这是对传统行事方式的恢复来美化激进变革的想法。

sentences.en: The idea that you dignify radical change by saying it's a restoration of traditional ways of doing things.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没有人能像克里斯提尼和他的支持者在这次事件中那样做得如此大胆和出色。

sentences.en: But I don't think anyone does it quite as boldly and brilliantly as Cleisthenes and his backers do on this occasion.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是他们发明或制度化关于雅典人来自大地等等故事的时刻吗？

sentences.en: Is this the point, Tom, where they invent or they institutionalise the story about
sentences.zh: 还是说这之前就存在了？

sentences.en: Athenians coming from the earth and all of that stuff?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or has that existed before?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这绝对是关键问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 为什么这个非常复杂的系统能如此迅速地被采纳？

sentences.en: So I think that's absolutely the key question.
sentences.zh: 部分原因显然是它实际上被证明是非常成功的。

sentences.en: How is it that this very complex system gets adopted so quickly?
sentences.zh: 所以你在本集开头读到的那段希罗多德的文字，是在庆祝斯巴达人尽管试图扑灭民主制度，

sentences.zh: 却无法做到，而且底比斯人在战斗中被击败的事实。

sentences.en: So that passage from Herodotus that you read at the beginning of the episode, that is celebrating the fact that the Spartans are unable to snuff out the democracy, even though
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，万岁，雅典民主不仅证明了它能守住阵地，而且实际上它还能主动出击。

sentences.en: they try to, and that Thebans get beaten in battle.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种微妙的感觉，你还记得歌德看着法国大革命的胜利军队时，认为这个过程释放了新的力量吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, hurrah, the Athenian democracy has demonstrated not only that it can hold its own, but that actually it can go on the attack.
sentences.zh: 但并没有人庆祝这是一个新事物。

sentences.en: So there's a slight sense there of, you remember Goethe looking at the victorious armies of the French Revolution and thinking, you know, new forces have been unleashed by this

sentences.en: process.
sentences.zh: 所以问题在于，克里斯提尼和所有人是否在编造雅典人是“土生土长”的、是从土壤中长出来的这种想法来证明其合理性？

sentences.en: But there is no celebration of the fact that this is new.
sentences.zh: 还是他顺应了雅典人已经相信的东西？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们有书面资料，比如追溯到梭伦，再往前就不多了。

sentences.en: Or is he going with the grain of things that the Athenians already believed?
sentences.zh: 我们有考古学证据表明，在公元前九世纪，阿提卡贫富之间的分歧确实在加剧。

sentences.en: And it's obviously quite difficult to do that because our sources are so scanty.
sentences.zh: 但所有关于忒修斯和厄瑞克透斯的东西，我的意思是，这显然不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, we have written sources, say, going back to Solon, not much before that.
sentences.zh: 那么它来自哪里呢？

sentences.en: We have archaeology that does show that in, say, the ninth century, divisions between rich and poor and Attica are growing much stronger.
sentences.zh: 我认为历史学家在理解这一点上的困难，恰恰就是我在本集开头所说的，

sentences.en: But all the stuff about
sentences.zh: 我们很难回到那种心态，去理解“德莫斯”对雅典人意味着什么。

sentences.en: Theseus and Erechtheus, I mean, this is clearly not true.

sentences.zh: 我认为它比那要奇怪得多。

sentences.zh: 和你在一起总是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Because it's not the people in the way that, you know, we might use it today, the people's party or the people's choice or the people say this.
sentences.zh: 和你在一起总是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's much, much weirder, I think, than that.
sentences.zh: 和你在一起总是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: It always is with you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 和你在一起总是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's never less weird.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉永远不会变得不那么怪异。

sentences.en: I pine.
sentences.zh: 我渴望着。

sentences.en: I look forward to the day when you do an episode and you say, the true story is much less strange and in no way weird.
sentences.zh: 我期待着有那么一天，当你做一期节目时，你会说，真实的故事远没有那么离奇，一点也不怪异。

sentences.en: So this is one of the key reasons why I ended up writing Dominion, was the difficulty of getting to grips with what Deimos actually meant to the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最终写出《多米尼恩》的关键原因之一，就是很难理解“戴摩斯”（Deimos）对雅典人来说到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: Because the whole idea that it's rights-based is an absolute nonsense.
sentences.zh: 因为那种认为它是基于权利的观点完全是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: But what does Deimos mean?
sentences.zh: 但“戴摩斯”是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: And the reason why it's hard for us to get back into and kind of understand it is that we don't believe in the Greek gods.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以难以回溯并理解它，是因为我们不相信希腊神灵。

sentences.en: And we don't believe in the fact that there might be a kind of, dare I say, a sacral ecosystem in which the gods and the land and the people are kind of bound together.
sentences.zh: 我们也不相信可能存在一种——我敢说——神圣的生态系统，在这种系统中，神灵、土地和人民是紧密相连的。

sentences.en: And in which Athena, who is a virgin, is also a mother and a queen and a guardian.
sentences.zh: 在这种系统中，身为处女的雅典娜同时也是一位母亲、一位女王和一位守护者。

sentences.en: And that this is somehow to the Athenians kind of real.
sentences.zh: 而且对雅典人来说，这在某种程度上是真实的。

sentences.en: And so that passage that you read from the children's book, I think in that book, I get closer to it than I did in Persian Fire, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以你读的那段童书里的文字，我觉得在那本书里，我比在《波斯火》中更接近这种感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because I think that the Deimos is, it's the entirety of all the people in Athens who have been born, who are living and who will be born in the future.

sentences.en: Very Berkian idea there, Tom.

sentences.en: It's kind of like the turning of the seasons, that every year the season turns and the earth gives birth to vines and to wheat.

sentences.zh: 这是人们总是纠结的一点：啊，女性没有投票权。

sentences.en: the most controversial.

sentences.en: That's their role.

sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so the collapse of the Athenian democracy in the Peloponnesian War, and then again, before the Macedonians, people turn around and say, well, we told you so.
sentences.zh: 所以雅典民主在伯罗奔尼撒战争中崩溃，后来在马其顿人到来之前，人们回过头来说，好吧，我们早就告诉过你们了。

sentences.en: So it comes to be seen as an experiment not worth repeating.
sentences.zh: 所以它被视为一个不值得重复的实验。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that tees up brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个绝佳的话题。

sentences.en: My last question, which is, we now think that there is a tradition, a story of progress.
sentences.zh: 我的最后一个问题是，我们现在认为存在一种传统，一种进步的故事。

sentences.en: So, you know, Athens, then there's that business in Iceland, you know, England, the mother of parliaments, the United States Congress, you know, Martin Luther
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，雅典，然后是冰岛的那档子事，你知道，英格兰，议会之母，美国国会，你知道，马丁·路德·

sentences.en: King having his dream, that there is this story.
sentences.zh: 金实现了他的梦想，认为存在这样一个故事。

sentences.en: Is there any sense in which we can talk of a continuity, a living tradition that goes through history in which, no.
sentences.zh: 我们是否可以在某种意义上谈论一种连续性，一种贯穿历史的活生生的传统，不。

sentences.en: So basically, you're saying that people pick up Athenian democracy later and try and pretend it's a model for them.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你是说人们后来捡起雅典民主，试图假装它是他们的榜样。

sentences.en: Athenian democracy, once people start reading about it in the Renaissance and after, again, it serves aristocratic elites as a terrible warning of what happens.
sentences.zh: 雅典民主，一旦人们在文艺复兴时期及以后开始阅读它，它再次成为了贵族精英们的一个可怕警告，提醒他们会发生什么。

sentences.en: So in the 17th century,
sentences.zh: 所以在17世纪，

sentences.en: Thomas Hobbes says people shouldn't be reading about this because it just encourages them to have ideas above their station.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·霍布斯说人们不应该读这些东西，因为它只会鼓励他们产生超越自己身份的想法。

sentences.en: And he's thinking specifically about the English revolution.
sentences.zh: 他特别指的是英国革命。

sentences.en: He feels that the example of Athenian democracy has fed into the kind of regicidal instincts of the radicals in the civil war.
sentences.zh: 他认为雅典民主的例子助长了内战中激进分子的弑君本能。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens with the French revolution, that conservatives feel that the influence of the study of Greek democracy on the French revolution has been wholly negative.
sentences.zh: 法国大革命也是如此，保守派认为研究希腊民主对法国大革命的影响完全是负面的。

sentences.en: But as democracy in the modern sense comes to spread, so the understanding of democracy comes to improve.
sentences.zh: 但随着现代意义上的民主开始传播，对民主的理解也随之改善。

sentences.en: And people look back at Athens and start seeing it as a kind of, you know, a shining city on a hill.
sentences.zh: 人们回望雅典，开始将其视为一种，你知道，山巅之城。

sentences.en: You know, this is the great model.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是伟大的典范。

sentences.en: But this is an invention.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种发明。

sentences.en: Our relationship with the past is always creative.
sentences.zh: 我们与过去的关系总是创造性的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, it's a kaleidoscopic effect.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种万花筒效应。

sentences.en: In an era where systems of government have the name of democracy, it's inevitable that attitudes to the original democracy are going to change.
sentences.zh: 在一个政府体制冠以民主之名的时代，对原始民主的态度不可避免地会发生变化。

sentences.en: But it's also inevitable that we will look back at that original democracy as a precursor to ours, whereas in fact, it's not at all.
sentences.zh: 但同样不可避免的是，我们会回望那个原始民主，将其视为我们民主的前身，而事实上，它根本不是。

sentences.en: It's something very different.
sentences.zh: 它是非常不同的东西。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: What an interesting note on which to end, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是一个多么有趣的结束语啊。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating subject.
sentences.zh: 这是一个迷人的主题。

sentences.en: It's all about, because it's not just the story of democracies, it's the story of the invention of tradition,
sentences.zh: 这完全是因为，因为这不仅仅是民主的故事，这是发明传统的故事，

sentences.en: the invention of ancient Greece as a model, I suppose, which, you know, most people listening to
sentences.zh: 我想是发明了作为典范的古希腊，你知道，大多数听这个节目的人，

sentences.en: this, I think, will still think of the ancient Greeks as the, you know, the birthplace of civilization, a model for all the lovely things we have today.
sentences.zh: 我想，仍然会认为古希腊是，你知道，文明的摇篮，是我们今天所拥有的所有美好事物的典范。

sentences.en: And it's fascinating to hear that in your trademark style, made stranger and more weird.
sentences.zh: 听到你用你标志性的风格，把它讲得更陌生、更怪异，真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: Weirdness all round.
sentences.zh: 到处都是怪异。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you, everybody.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Tom, before you go, one more plug, please.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在你走之前，请再打个广告。

sentences.en: This is very, I mean, it's very unlike you, very unlikely.
sentences.zh: 这非常，我的意思是，这很不符合你的风格，非常不可能。

sentences.en: So if people want to read a book in which the gods are real, Greece is weird, people turn into bears, what's the name of that book, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们想读一本神是真实的、希腊很怪异、人会变成熊的书，那本书叫什么名字，汤姆？

sentences.zh: 《狼女、众神与希腊人》。
